documents.title: Generative AI @ WCU - A Guiding Framework
documents.summary: A long university framework from IS&T and the Teaching & Learning Center with six recommendations (follow policies, protect data, equity, verify accuracy, be transparent, keep informed). It is a living set of recommendations, not a policy, and tells faculty to state their own AI expectations.
documents.stance_why: The page says "This framework is a living document, not a university policy" and sets no ban or permission itself; it tells faculty to be "transparent about their expectations" and lets each instructor choose, even a complete prohibition, so the decision is delegated.

documents.title: Responsible Generative AI Use
documents.summary: A short IS&T page defining generative AI and giving role-based responsible-use points for faculty, staff and students. It repeatedly sends students to the course instructor's policy and ties use to integrity policy.
documents.stance_why: It says "Always check with course instructors about when it is appropriate to use generative AI tools. It is the responsibility of the student to know and follow the course policy", handing the decision to each course.

notes: No school or computing-unit policy found; course layer deferred. The framework page states it is not a university policy. Both coders found no new types; coder B's candidate (advice to instructors on how to justify and communicate a policy) was mapped to P66 with a fit_note, and the 'no dedicated AI Center' fact stays UNCOVERED. Coder notes: A: the last framework unit (appendix table) anchors on sample acknowledgment wording. B: the optional disclosure ('It is your decision ... to disclose') sits next to 'Be transparent about AI usage', so disclosure is recommended but not required unless a course says so; the First Year Experience 'Use AI' statement repeats statement 1 and was not coded again. Reconciliation dropped four exact repeats that coder A coded (FYE 'withhold a grade', Nursing rationale, Nursing 'Failure to acknowledge', Nursing 'Submitted work may be reviewed'), consistent with the rule on exact repeats; their fit notes duplicated those of the first occurrences.
